cases.input: One ERP product has Finance, Procurement and HR applications with distinct keys, owners and criticality.
cases.expect: Three BusinessApplication identities reference the shared product without identity collapse.

cases.input: Procurement spans two installations for different organizational contexts.
cases.expect: One application has two effective usage or installation bindings and retains one application identity.

cases.input: A SaaS application is used by one business unit with no local installation.
cases.expect: ApplicationUsage records hosted delivery explicitly and no local installation is fabricated.

cases.input: A purchased licence automatically creates an installation and application record.
cases.expect: The inference is rejected because entitlement, deployment and application are separate lifecycles.

cases.input: The vendor product name is reused as system, application and installation key.
cases.expect: The records are rejected until each governed layer has its own identity and master.

cases.input: A separately licensed module is automatically promoted to a BusinessApplication.
cases.expect: Promotion is blocked until a dated decision assigns its own application key, purpose and owner.

cases.input: Deploying the same release in a second region creates a second Software Product and BusinessApplication.
cases.expect: The clones are rejected; only a new deployment occurrence and runtime binding are created.
